⚠️WARNING: This post describes a major natural disaster and mass casualty event.

A massive evacuation is underway in the Philippines as the country braces for Super Typhoon Fung-wong (locally named Uwan), which is expected to make landfall on Sunday evening.

More than 900,000 people have been ordered to evacuate as the storm, with sustained winds of 185 km/h (115mph) and gusts up to 230km/h (143mph), bears down on the Bicol region and the main island of Luzon.

This new disaster comes just days after Typhoon Kalmaegi (locally named Tino) devastated the central Philippines, causing catastrophic flooding and landslides.

Kalmaegi Death Toll: The death toll from Kalmaegi has risen to at least 204 people, with over 100 still missing.

Helicopter Crash: A military helicopter deployed for relief efforts for the first storm crashed on Tuesday, killing all six crew members aboard.

A state of calamity has been declared, and nearly 300 flights have been canceled in anticipation of Super Typhoon Fung-wong.

Evacuation Update as of November 9, 2025 | 4:00 PM

Bilang pag-iingat sa pagbaha na sanhi ng mga pag-ulan dulot ng Bagyong #UwanPH, mayroong itinalagang evacuation sites sa mga piling lugar na bahain o may banta ng landslide para sa ligtas at mabilis na paglikas.

Sa kasalukuyan, nasa 1,213 pamilya o 4,047 indibidwal ang inilikas at namamalagi sa evacuation sites sa ating lungsod. 

Para sa emergency, tumawag sa Quezon City HELPLINE 122.
